Subcomponent 1.2 will finance activities to improve the availability and quality of social statistics This subcomponent includes activities related to an annual labor force survey, a household survey, a population and housing census, cartography and geospatial data collection, gender statistics, and other relevant activities.
According to the PHC 2025 plan prepared by UNFPA, two digital innovations will be introduced to the PHC 2025: i) CAPI data collection; and ii) digital census maps.
These digital enumeration maps will be installed on the tablets and integrated with the digital questionnaires.

The project will finance a purchase of high-resolution satellite images and consultancy to support the production of the census cartography – the geocoded maps of housing, health facilities, schools, forests, and infrastructures aimed to be used as basis for gathering census information on site.

These maps can be used for evaluating risk-prone areas and access to public services and enabling a better and more targeted policy response in the event of natural hazards and more accurate estimation of household’s exposure to climate change.
The activity will form the fundamental geospatial architecture embedded in administrative and survey data collection activities in the LSS.
This activity will pilot an integrated data platform hosted by LSB.

The platform will be designed and implemented to store census and survey data collected by the LSB, and selected administrative data from line ministries including the MoF, MPI, MoIC, MoHA, BoL, and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MoLSW), and selected administrative data from provincial statistics sections in Vientiane Capital, Oudomxay, Vientiane, and Champassak.

Priority will be given to line ministries and provincial statistics sections whose information system is well-developed or has been supported by the World Bank projects (Figure 2 and Table 4).20 Under this activity, the project will finance consultancy services to design, build and implement the platform.
A centralized data portal will be set up as a one-stop shop where public users can access data and statistics.
The activity also includes integrating or linking the existing but fragmented portals (www.lsb.gov.la, LAOSIS, SDG Open data, LAOINFO).
The portal will build on the integrated data platform (Activity 2.1.1) and use data visualization to enhance data dissemination and make data access easier and more user friendly.
For example, an interface for labor market monitoring can be developed utilizing labor force survey data and administrative data from the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare.
Microdata library will be included providing a catalog, documentation, and access to public-use and restricted-use microdata files.
